mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 2% year-over-year, observed at the decision date, signals weakening aggregate demand and reduces expected corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% at decision date
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, combined with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10%, signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity that depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: If the mechanism fails to produce negative 20-day returns in at least 70% of co-triggered months, it is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recessionary regime (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive monetary easing intended to stimulate growth, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < 0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, combined with a simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4%, signals an overheating labor market that precedes a policy tightening; this combination predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market before monetary tightening
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of co-triggered months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is rejected.
